information  for  citizens  to  secure  access  to  information  under  the  control  of  public  authorities, 
in  order  to  promote  transparency  and  accountability  in  the  working  of  every  public  authority, 
and  whereas  the  attached  publication  of  the  Bureau  of  Indian  Standards  is  of  particular  interest 
to  the  public,  particularly  disadvantaged  communities  and  those  engaged  in  the  pursuit  of 
education  and  knowledge,  the  attached  public  safety  standard  is  made  available  to  promote  the 
timely  dissemination  of  this  information  in  an  accurate  manner  to  the  public.

SPECIFICATION  FOR 
HOT-DIP  TERNE  COATED  CARBON  STEEL  SHEETS

1.  Scope  —  Covers  the  requirements  of  terne  coated  carbon  steel  sheets  of  thicknees  from  0*3  to 

2  0  mm  for  use  in  automobile  industry,  and  as  a  roofing  material  and  similar  other  applications. 

2.  Definitions  and  Other  Information  —  For  the  purpose  of  this  standard,  the  following  definition 
shall  apply. 

2.1  Continuous  Hot-Dip  Terne  (  Lead  Alloy  )  Coated  Cold-Reduced  Steel  Sheet  —  A  product  obtai- 
ned by  hot-dip  coating  cold-reduced  sheet  coils  on  a  continuous  lead  alloy  coating  line  to  produce 
either  lead  alloy  coated  coils  or  lead  alloy  coated  cut  lengths. 

2.2  Terne  (  Lead  Alloy )  —  In  the  context  of  this  Standard,  any  lead-based  alloy  In  commercial  use 
for  the  hot-dip  coating  of  steel  sheet.  Tin  is  the  most  common  alloying  element,  but  antimony  is  also 
commercially  used,  are  combinations  of  both  elements  If  a  specific  alloy  composition  Is  required, 
it  shall  be  by  agreement  between  the  manufacturer  and  the  purchaser. 

2.3  Designation  System  —  Terne  Coating  and  Qualities  —  The  produced  hot-dip  terne  coating  is 
designated  TO  ( the  '0*  is  inserted  to  fill  a  computer  space  and  has  no  significance  in  the  designa- 
tion )  as  shown  In  Table  1.  The  coating  mass  designation  follows  the  TO  and  three  spaces  are  allo- 
cated for  coating  mass  designation.  If  only  two  spaces  are  required,  such  as  for  designation  75', 
then  the  75'  Is  preceded  by  a  '0'  to  fill  computer  space  and  is  shown  as  '075*.  If  the  product  is 
skin  passed,  designation  'S'  is  used  to  indicate  the  coating  condition.  If  the  product  has  not  been 
skin  passed,  the  designation  'N'  for  normal  coating  (  as  produced  )  is  shown.  The  numbers  01,  02, 

03  and  04  are  common  to  other  standards  indicatjng  the  qualities  of  commercial,  drawing,  deep 
drawing,  and  deep  drawing  special  killed.  An  example  of  a  complete  condition  designation  includ- 
ing coating,  coating  mass,  coating  condition  and  quality  is  TO  120N01.  This  is  composed  'by 
combining  the  following: 

TO   »  terne  coating 

120  »  coating  designation  (  see  Table  2  ) 

N     »  normal  coating 

01     —  ordinary  quality 

2.4  Skin  Pass  —  A  light  cold  rolling  of  terne  sheet.  The  purposes  of  skin  passing  are  one  or  more 
of  the  following: 

a)  To  minimize  temporarily  the  occurrence  of  conditions  known  as  stretcher  strain  (  Luder's 
lines  )  or  fluting  during  fabrication  of  finished  parts. 

b)  To  control  shape. 

c)  To  produce  a  higher  degree  of  surface  smoothness  and  to  Improve  appearance  or  suitabi- 
lity for  decorative  painting.  This  process  may  adversely  affect  the  ductility  of  the  base  metal. 

2.5  Strain  Ageing  —  Terne  sheet  (  except  TO  04  )  tends  to  strain  age.  Grade  TO  04  should  be  speci- 
fied where  strain  ageing  Is  not  acceptable  and  where  roller  levelling  is  not  possible. 

2.6  Oiling  —  Terne  sheet  Is  produced  either  oiled  or  not  oiled,  and  Is  usually  not  degreased. 


Adopted  25  February  1988

3.  Conditions  of  IManufacture 

3.1  Steelmaking  —  The  process  used  in  making  steel  and  in  manufacturing  terne  sheet  should  be 
agreed  between  the  manufacturer  and  the  purchaser. 

3.2  Ladle  Analysis  —  The  ladle  analysis  of  steel,  when  carried  out  either  by  the  method  specified  in 
relevant  parts  of  IS  :  228  'Methods  for  chemical  analysis  of  steel  { second  revision  Y  (  issued  in 
parts  )  or  any  other  established  Instrumental/chemical  method,  shall  be  as  given  in  Table  1.  In  case 
of  any  dispute,  the  procedure  given  In  relevant  parts  of  IS  :  228  shall  be  the  referee  method.

3.3  Product  Analysis  —  Permissible  variation  in  the  case  of  product  analysis  from  the  limits  speci- 
fied in  Table  1  shall  be  given  as  below: 

Constituent  Permissible  Variation  Over

Note  1  —  The  requirements  regarding  permisaibie  variation  on  product  anaiysis  shall  not  apply  to  rimming 
steels. 

Note  2  —  When  the  steel  is  Iciiied  with  aluminium,  the  total  soluble  aluminium  In  steel  shall  be  between  0*02 
and  0*6  percent,  which  shall  be  ensured  by  the  manufacturer  by  occasional  checl^s. 

Note  3  —  When  the  steel  Is  rimming  or  semi-killed  or  is  not  fully  l(itied  by  aluminium  alone,  nitrogen  content 
shall  not  exceed  0*007  percent.    This  should  be  ensured  by  occasional  checit  analysis. 

Note  4  —  When  the  steel  Is  silicon  killed,  the  silicon  content  on  analysis  shall  not  be  less  than  0*1  percent. 
When  the  steel  Is  silicon-aluminium  or  aluminium  killed,  the  requirement  regarding  minimum  silicon  content  shall 
not  apply. 

Note  5 » The  material  may  be  supplied  in  the  copper  bearing  quality  in  which  case  the  copper  shall  be 
between  0*20  and  0*35  percent  on  analysis.    On  product  analysis,  this  shall  be  between  0*17  and  0*38  percent. 

3.4  Terne  (  Lead  Alloy  )  Coating  l\4ass  —  The  mass  of  coating  shall  conform  to  the  requirements  in 
Table  2  for  the  specific  coating  designation.  The  mass  of  coating  Is  the  total  amount  on  both  sur- 
faces of  the  sheet,  expressed  in  grams  per  square  metre  (  g/m' )  of  sheet.  Methods  of  checking 
that  the  material  complies  with  this  standard  are  given  in  5.2, 6.2  and  Appendix  A.  Procedures  other 
than  those  covered  in  Appendix  A  may  be  permitted  upon  agreement  by  the  manufacturer  and  the 
purchaser.

3.5  Application  —  It  is  desirable  that  terne  sheet  be  identified  for  fabrication  by  name  of  the  part 
or  by  the  intended  application.  Terne  sheet  of  drawing  qualities  (  TO  02,  TO  03  and  TO  04  )  may  be 
produced  to  make  an  identified  part  within  a  properly  established  breakage  allowance,  which  shall 
be  previously  agreed  upon  between  the  producer  and  the  purchaser.  In  this  case,  the  part  name, 
the  details  of  fabrication  and  special  requirements  ( that  is,  exposed  or  unexposed,  freedom  from 
stretcher 4tra ins  or  fluting,  coating  performance  requirements  )  shall  be  specified  and  the  mechani- 
cal properties  given  in  Table  3  shall  not  apply. 

3.6  Mechanical  Properties  —  Except  when  ordered  to  an  identified  part  as  explained  in  3.5  at  the 
time  that  the  steel  is  made  available  for  shipment,  the  mechanical  properties  shall  be  as  stated  in 
Table  3  when  they  are  determined  on  test  pieces  obtained  according  to  the  requirements  of  6.1. 

Note  —  Prolonged  storage  of  tlie  eiieet  after  eldn  passing  can  cause  a  change  In  mechanical  properties  and 
increase  In  drawabillty.    To  minlnoize  this  effect,  quality  T0704  should  be  specified.

4.  Dimensional  Tolerances  —  Tolerance  limits  for  terne  sheet  are  shown  in  Tables  5  to  13. 

5.  Sampling 

5.1  Mechanical  Tests 

5.1.1  Tensile  test  —  When  ordered  to  mechanical  properties,  one  representative  sample  for  the 
tensile  property  test  required  in  Table  3  shall  be  taken  from  each  lot  of  shipment.  A  lot  consists  of 
SO  tonnes  or  less  of  sheet  of  the  same  quality  rolled  to  the  same  thickness  and  condition. 

5.1.2  Bend  test —  One  representative  sample  for  the  bend  test  (applicable  only  to  quality  TO 
01  )  shall  be  taken  from  each  lot  (  see  5.1.1  )  of  sheet  for  shipment. 

5.2  Coating  Tests 

5.2.1  Mass  of  coating  —  The  producer  shall  malte  such  tests  and  measurements  as  he  deems 
necessary  to  ensure  that  the  material  produced  compiles  with  the  values  in  Table  2.  The  purchaser 
may  verify  the  mass  of  coating  by  the  following  sampling  method. 

Three  specimens  shall  be  cut,  one  from  the  mid  width  position,  and  one  from  each  side  not 
closer  than  2S  mm  from  the  side  edge.  The  minimum  specimen  area  should  be  2  000  mm^ 

5.2.2  Bend  test  —  One  representative  sample  shall  be  taken  from  each  lot  of  sheet  for  shipment. 
The  specimens  should  be  taken  for  the  coated  bend  test,  not  closer  than  25  mm  from  the  side  edge. 
The  minimum  specimen  width  should  be  50  mm. 

6.  Test  Methods 

••1  Mechanical  Tests 

6.1.1  Tensile  test  ( base  metal)  •—  The  tensile  test  shall  be  performed  In  accordance  with  IS :  1663- 
1972  'Method  for  tensile  testing  of  steel  sheet  and  strip  of  thickness  0*5  mm  to  3  mm  (  first  revi- 
sion )\  Transverse  or  longitudinal  test  pieces  shall  be  taken  mid  way  between  the  centre  and  edge 
of  the  sheet  as  rolled.  Since  the  tensile  test  is  for  determination  of  properties  of  the  base  metal, 
ends  of  test  pieces  should  be  stripped  of  the  coating  to  measure  base  metal  thickness  for  calcu- 
lation of  cross  sectional  area. 


18:12313-1988 

6.1.2  Bend  test  ( base  metal )  ( applicable  only  to  quality  TO  01  )  —  The  transverse  bend  test 
piece,  stripped  of  coating  in  a  suitably  inhibited  acid,  shall  withstand  being  bent  through  180''  In  the 
direction  shown  in  Fig.  1,  around  the  inside  diameter  as  shown  In  Table  3  without  cracking  on  the 
outside  of  the  bent  portion.  The  bend  test  shall  be  performed  at  ambient  temperature  and  as  des- 
cribed in  IS  :  1599-1985  'Method  for  bend  test  (  second  revision  )'. 

6.2  Coating  Tests 

6.2.1  Triple  spot  test  —  The  triple  spot  test  result  Is  the  average  coating  mass  found  on  the  three 
pieces  taken  according  to  5.2.1.  The  testis  normally  carried  out  by  stamping  out  a  known  area  of 
sheet  and  calculating  the  coating  mass  from  the  loss  in  mass  after  removing  the  terne  (  lead  alloy  ) 
coating  in  suitably  Inhibited  acid  (  see  Appendix  A  for  suggested  methods  ).  Procedures  other  than 
those  in  Appendix  A  may  be  permitted  upon  agreement  by  the  manufacturer  and  the  purchaser. 


FIG.  1    TRANSVERSE  BEND  TEST  PIECE  (  After  Bending  ) 

6.2.2  Single  spot  test  —  The  single  spot  test  result  shall  be  the  minimum  coating  mass  found  on 
any  one  of  the  three  specimens  used  for  the  triple  spot  test.  Material  slit  from  wide  coil  will  be 
subject  to  a  single  spot  test. 

6.2.3  Bend  test  (  coating  )  —  Bend  test  pieces  taken  after  coating  ( before  additional  processing  ) 
shall  withstand  being  bent  through  180""  in  either  direction  without  flaking  of  the  coating  on  the 
outside  of  the  bend.  The  radius  of  the  bend  is  determined  by  the  number  of  pieces  of  the  same 
thickness  (  or  mandrel  equivalent )  as  shown  In  Table  4.  Flaking  of  coating  within  7  mm  from  the 
edge  of  the  specimen  shall  not  be  cause  for  rejection. 

TABLE  4    COATING  BEND  TEST  REQUIREMENTS

7.  RetMts  —  If  a  test  does  not  give  the  required  results,  two  more  tests  shall  be  carried  out  at  a 
random  on  the  same  lot  Both  retests  must  conform  to  the  requirements  of  this  standard,  otherwise 
the  lot  may  be  rejected. 


IS  :  12313  •  1988 

8.  Workmanship  —  The  terne  sheet  In  cut  lengths  shall  be  free  from  amounts  of  laminations, 
surface  flaws  and  other  Imperfections  that  are  detrimental  to  subsequent  appropriate  processing. 
Processing  for  shipment  in  coils  does  not  afford  the  producer  the  opportunity  to  observe  readily  or 
to  remove  defective  portions  as  can  be  carried  out  on  the  cut  length  product.  An  excessive  number 
of  defects  may  be  the  cause  of  reiection. 

9.  Inspection  and  Acceptance 

9.1  While  not  usually  required  for  products  covered  by  this  standard,  when  the  purchaser  specifies 
that  inspection  and  tests  for  acceptance  be  observed  prior  to  shipment  from  the  manufacturer's 
worlds,  the  manufacturer  shall  provide  the  purchaser's  inspector  all  reasonable  facilities  to  deter- 
mine that  the  sheet  is  being  furnished  in  accordance  with  this  standard. 

9.2  Terne  sheet  that  is  reported  to  be  defective  after  arrival  at  the  user's  works  shall  be  set  aside 
properly  and  correctly  identified  and  adequately  protected.  The  supplier  shall  be  notified  in  order 
that  he  may  properly  investigate. 

10.  Coil  Size  -—  When  terne  sheet  is  ordered  In  coils,  a  minimum  or  range  of  acceptable  inside 
diameter  (  ID. )  shall  be  specified,  in  addition,  the  maximum  outside  diameter  (  O.D. )  and  maxi- 
mum acceptable  coil  mass  shall  be  specified. 

11.  IMarking  —  Unless  otherwise  stated,  the  following  minimum  requirements  for  identifying  the 
terne  sheet  shall  be  legibly  stenciled  on  the  top  of  each  lift  or  shown  on  a  tag  attached  to  each  coil 
or  shipping  unit: 

a)  Manufacturer's  name  or  trade-marl(, 

b)  Quality  designation, 

c)  Coating  designation, 

d)  Product  dimensions, 

e)  Lot  number,  and 

f)  Mass. 

11.1  Standard  Marking  —  Details  available  with  the  Bureau  of  Indian  Standards. 

12.  Information  to  be  Supplied  by  the  Purchaser 

12.1  To  specify  adequately  the  requirements  under  this  Standard,  inquiries  and  orders  shall 
include  the  following  Information: 

a)  Number  of  this  standard; 

b)  Name,  coating  designation,  coating  condition  and  quality  of  material  [  for  example,  terne 
sheet  (TO  120  NO  2)  see  2.3]; 

c)  Dimensions  of  product  ( the  thickness  includes  the  coating  )  and  quantity  required; 

d)  Application  (  name  of  part  or  intended  usage  ),  if  possible  (  see  3.5 ); 

e)  For  drawing  qualities  TO  02,  TO  03,  TO  04,  whether  ordered  to  mechanical  properties  ( see 
3.9  )  or  to  fabricate  on  Identified  part  ( see  3.5 ); 

f)  Oiled,  if  required  ( see  2.9  ); 

g)  Coil  size  requirements  (  see  10  ); 

h)  Report  of  cast  analysis,  if  required; 

j)  Details  of  fabrication  or  special  requirements  (  fluting  or  coating  performance);  and 

k)  Inspection  and  tests  for  acceptance  prior  to  shipment  from  the  producer's  works,  if  requi- 
red (  see  9.1  ).

APPENDIX     A 

(  Clauses  3.4  and  6.2.1  ) 

DETERMINATION  OF  MASS  AND  COMPOSITION  OF  COATING  ON 
TERNE  (  LEAD  ALLOY  )  COATED  SHEET 

A-1.  General 

A-1.1  This  appendix  covers  the  determination  of  the  mass  and  composition  of  coating  on  terne 
sheets  by  the  triple  spot  method.  Five  procedures  are  described  as  follovyrs: 

a)  Procedure  A  :  Stripping  with  sulphuric  acid, 

b)  Procedure  B  :  Electrolytic  stripping, 

c)  Procedure  C  :  Stripping  with  silver  nitrate  solution, 

d)  Procedure  D  :  Stripping  with  hydrochloric  acid  and  antimony  (  III )  chloride,  and 

e)  Procedure  E  :  Stripping  with  sodium  hydroxide  and  sodium  peroxide. 

A-1.2  If  the  percentage  of  tin  or  lead  or  both  In  the  coating  Is  required,  stripping  with  sulphuric 
acid  is  the  preferred  procedure.  Electrolytic  strippping  and  stripping  with  silver  nitrate  or  anti- 
mony (  III  )  chloride  or  sodium  hydroxide  and  sodium  peroxide  are  convenient  procedures  where  a 
large  number  of  determinations  of  mass  of  coating  are  to  be  made. 

A-2.  Test  Specimens 

A-2.1  Test  specimens  shall  be  stamped  or  cut  from  the  sheet,  usually  from  the  centre  and  near 
both  edges. 

A-2.2  Specimens  shall  be  50  ±  0*25  mm  square  56*42  db  0'25  mm  in  diameter  except  that  for  mate- 
rial narrower  than  50  mm  in  width,  test  specimens  shall  be  of  such  a  length  that  the  area  of  the 
specimen  is  equal  to  2  500  mm*.  The  mass  of  coating  in  grams  on  a  specimen  SO  mm  square  (2  500 
mm*  in  area  )  when  multiplied  by  400  is  equal  to  the  mass  of  coating  in  grams  per  square  metre  of 
sheet.  When  it  is  not  possible  to  secure  a  specimen  of  2  500  mm'  In  area,  a  smaller  size  may  be 
used,  but  it  is  recommended  that  a  specimen  of  not  less  than  2  000  mm'  be  used. 

A-*2.3  The  specimens  shall  be  clean,  if  necessary,  they  shall  be  washed  with  solvent  naphtha  or 
other  suitable  solvent,  then  with  alcohol  and  dried  thoroughly. 

A*3.  Procedure  A  —  Stripping  with  Sulphuric  Acid 

A-3.1  Reagents  —  Reagent  grade  chemicals  shall  be  used  in  all  tests.  Other  grades  may  be  used, 
provided  it  Is  first  ascertained  that  the  reagent  is  of  sufficiently  high  purity  to  permit  its  use  without 
lessening  the  accuracy  of  the  determination. 

A-3.1.1  Cerium  (IV)  sulphate  —  Standard  volumetric  solution   (1  ml  A  0005  6  g  Fe,  01  N). 
Prepare  and  standardize  so  that  the  solution  will  be  0*1  N. 

A-3.1.2  Erioglaucine    Indicator  —  Prepare  a  0*1  percent  (  mim  )  solution  of  erioglaucine  A  in 
water. 

A-3.1.3  Hydrochloric  add.  p  1.12  gjml  —  Mix  500  ml  of  cp  or  reagent  grade   hydrochloric  acid 
(  p  1.19  g/ml )  with  400  ml  of  distilled  water. 

A-3.1.4  Mercury    {II)  chloride  solution  (SO  gil )  —  Dissolve  50  g  of  mercury   (  II  )  chloride 
(  HgCIs )  In  water  and  dilute  to  1  litre. 

A-3.1.5  Potassium  iodate  —  Standard  volumetric  solution  (1  ml  A  0003  gSn,  ,0'05N).  Prepare  and 
standardize  so  that  the  solution  will  be  0*05  N. 

A-3.1.6  Potassium  permanganate  saturated  solution 

A-3.1.7  Sodium  hydrogen  carbonate,   saturated  solution  —  Saturate  freshly  boiled  distilled  water 
with  sodium  hydrogen  carbonate  (  NaHCOs ). 

A-3.1.8  Sodium  hydrogen  carbonate  1  percent  (  wjv  )  —  Dissolve  about  10  g  of  sodium  hydrogen 
carbonate  (  NaHCOs )  In  1  litre  of  freshly  boiled  distilled  water. 

A.3.1.9  r//i  (//)   chloride    solution  —  Dissolve     150  g   of     tin    (II)    chloride     dihydrate 
( SnCI|2HtO )  In  1  litre  of  hydrochloric  add,  diluted  1  +2  (  V+V  ). 


IS  :  12313  -  1988 

A-3.1.10  Starch  solution 

A-3.1.11  Sulphuric  add  —  p  1-84  g/ml,  cp  or  reagent  grade. 

A-3.2  Procedure  for  Stripping  —  Accurately  determine  the  mass  of  each  test  specimen  In  grams. 
Wrap  a  stiff  platinum  or  nickel  wire  about  each  specimen  in  such  a  manner  that  it  may  be  held 
firmly  in  an  acid  solution  in  a  horizontal  position  Using  a  400-ml  beaker,  heat  60  ml  of  the  sulphuric 
acid  ( A-3.1.11  )  to  250''C  ( see  Caution  ).  Immerse  each  specimen  for  about  1  min  In  the  hot 
acid;  then  remove  and  momentarily  immerse  In  SO  ml  of  distilled  water  contained  in  a  600  ml 
beaker.  Rub  the  surface  of  the  specimen  with  a  rubber  tipped  glass  rod  while  washing  with  about 
SO  ml  of  distilled  water  from  a  wash  bottle.  If  the  coating  has  not  been  completely  removed,  again 
Immerse  in  the  acid  and  repeat  the  procedure.  Thoroughly  dry  and  reweigh  the  specimen.  The  loss 
in  mass,  Am,  represents  the  mass  of  coating,  together  with  some  iron  dissolved  from  the  steel 
sheet. 

CAUTION  —  A  suitable  face    shield  should  be  worn  in  order  to  protect  the  operator  from 
accidental  splashing  or  popping  of  hot  sulphuric  acid. 

A-3.3  Chemical  Analysis 

A-3.3.1  Test  solution  —Cool  the  sulphuric  acid  solution  in  which  the  specimen  was  stripped 
and  combine  with  the  washings  obtained  in  the  600*ml  beaker  while  stripping  the  specimen.  Pour 
the  solution  into  a  500-ml  volumetric  flask  and  rinse  the  beaker  with  hydrochloric  acid  (A-3.1.3). 
Add  the  rinsing  to  the  flask  and  dilute  to  the  SOO  ml  mark  with  hydrochloric  acid  (  A-3.1.3  ),  again 
diluting  to  the  mark  after  cooling,  If  necessary.  The  solution  may  now  be  analysed  for  Iron  and,  If 
desired,  lead  and  tin. 

A-3.3.2  Determination  of  Iron  —  Transfer  100  ml  aliquot  of  the  solution  in  the  SOO-ml  volu- 
metric flask  (  see  A-3.3.1  )  to  a  600-ml  beaker.  Add  1  to  2  ml  of  the  saturated  potassium  permang- 
anate solution  (  A-3.1.6  )  to  oxidize  Iron  and  tin,  and  heat  to  boiling.  Cool  and  add  slight  excess  of 
ammonia.  Filter  and  wash  the  precipitate  with  hot  water.  Dissolve  the  precipitate  In  the  original 
beaker  with  hydrochloric  acid  (  A-3.1.3  )  and  hot  water.  Evaporate  the  solution  to  a  volume  of  about 
10  ml  and  reduce  with  the  tin  (  II )  chloride  solution  (  A-3.1.9).  Add  10  ml  of  the  mercury  ( II ) 
chloride  solution  (  A-3.1.4  )  and  400  ml  of  water.  Titrate  with  the  standard  volumetric  cerium  ( IV  ) 
sulphate  solution  ( A-3.1.1  )  using  erioglaucine  (  A-3.1.2  )  as  Indicator.  Calculate  the  mass,  mtt,  in 
grams  of  iron  dissolved  from  the  test  specimen  using  the  formula: 

nife  ^  SmiVi 

where 

Vi  -"  volume  In  milliiitres  of  the  standard  volumetric  cerium  ( IV  )  sulphate  solution  requi- 
red for  the  titration,  and 

mi  -»  mass  in  grams  of  iron  equivalent  to  1  ml  of  the  standard  volumetric  cerium   (  IV  ) 
sulphate  solution. 

A-3.3.3  Determination  of  tin  —  Transfer  200  ml  aliquot  of  the  test  solution  (  see  A-3.3.1  )  to 
a  300-ml  Erienmeyer  flask.  Add  3  g  of  Iron  in  the  form  of  fine  wire  or  thin  sheet  and  1  g  of  pow- 
dered antimony.  Fit  the  flask  with  a  one-hole  rubber  stopper  containing  a  glass  tube  bent  twice  at 
right  angles,  with  the  end  of  the  short  bend  projecting  through  the  stopper,  the  other  end  being  long 
enough  to  reach  almost  to  the  bottom  of  a  beaker  placed  on  a  level  with  the  flask.  Pour  about  300 
ml  of  the  dilute  sodium  hydrogen  carbonate  solution  (  A-3.1.8  )  Into  that  beaker.  Place  the  flask  on 
a  hot*plate,  with  the  glass  tube  extending  Into  the  beaker.  After  boiling  the  solution  In  the  flask  for 
about  S  min,  remove  the  beaker  containing  the  dilute  sodium  hydrogen  carbonate  solution  and 
substitute  by  another  beaker  containing  about  SO  ml  of  the  saturated  sodium  hydrogen  carbonate 
solution  (  A-3.1.7  ).  Move  both,  the  beaker  and  the  flask,  to  a  cool  place.  This  will  cause  a  small 
amount  of  the  saturated  sodium  hydrogen  carbonate  solution  to  enter  the  flask  and  exclude  the  air. 
Finally  cool  the  solution  In  the  flask  to  about  8-10*C.  Add  several  mlllllltres  of  the  starch 
solution  ( A-3.1.10 )  and  titrate  with  the  standard  potassium  lodate  solution  ( A-3.1.S ).  It  Is  desirable 
to  run  a  duplicate  analysis  for  tin  adding  the  standard  potassium  lodate  solution  quickly  to  a  point 
slightly  less  than  the  end  point  obtained  In  the  previous  determination.  Then  finish  the  titration  more 
slowly.  This  duplicate  analysis  may  be  run  using  one  or  the  other  test  specimens.  Calculate  the 
mass  mgn  in  grams,  of  tin  stripped  from  the  test  specimen  using  the  formula: 

/Hea  —  2 

10

where

A-3.3.4  Determination  of  lead  —  After  ascertaining  that  all  the  lead  (  II )  chloride  is  in  the  solu- 
tion, remove  a  100  ml  aliquot  from  the  500  ml  volumetric  flask  (  see  A-3.3*1  )  and  place  in  a  400  ml 
beaker.  Add  10  ml  of  the  sulphuric  acid  (  A-3.1.11  ),  cover  and  evaporate  to  fumes  of  sulphur  tri- 
oxide.  Cool  and  dilute  to  200  ml  with  water.  Allow  to  settle  and  then  filter  on  weighed  Gooch 
crucible,  washing  with  sulphuric  acid,  diluted  1  +  19  (  1^  +  /  ).  Dry  and  ignite  at  a  dull  red  heat. 
Cool  and  rewelgh.  Calculate  the  mass,  /7?pb  in  grams,  of  lead  stripped  from  the  test  specimen  using 
the  formula: 

mpb  —  5  (  ma  —  /n4 )  x  0  683  1 

where 

mi  »  mass,  in  grams,  of  the  Gooch  crucible  and  ignited  precipitate,  and 
mi  ">  mass.  In  grams,  of  the  Gooch  crucible. 

A-3.4  Calculations 

A-3.4.1  Mass  of  coating 

Calculate  the  mass  of  coating  in  grams  per  square  metre  using  the  formula: 

400  (  Am  -  mtt ) 

where

specimen  of  2  500  mm*  in  area  Is  used.  For  specimens  of  other  sizes,  a  suitable 
correction  factor  shall  be  applied. 

A-3.4.2  Percentage  of  tin  In  coating  —  Calculate  the  percentage,  by  mass,  of  tin    in  the  coating 
using  the  formula:

A-3.4.3  Percentage  of  lead  In  coaZ/nfif  —  Calculate  the  percentage  of  lead   in    the  coating  by 
subtracting  the  percentage  of  tin  (  see  A-3.4.2  )  from  100  percent. 

A-4.  Procedure  B  —  Electrolytic  Stripping 

A-4.1  Reagents 

A-4.1.1  Hydrochloric  add  —  diluted  1  +  3  (  1^  +  1/  )  —  Mix  1  part  of  cp  or  reagent  grade  hydro- 
chloric acid  (  p  1*19  g/ml )  with  3  parts  of  water. 

A-4.1.2  Sodium  hydroxide  solution  —  Dissolve  100  g  of  sodium  hydroxide  (  NaOH  )  in  distilled 
water  and  dilute  to  1  litre. 

A-4.2  Procedure  for  stripping  —  After  cleaning  the  test  specimens  as  described  in  A-2.3 
weigh  each  specimen  separately.  Strip  anodically  in  the  sodium  hydroxide  solution  (  A-4.1.2  }  at  a 
temperature  of  77  to  80^C  for  10  to  12  min,  or  until  the  coating  Is  completely  removed,  using  a  cur- 
rent of  4  A.  Reverse  the  current  for  6  to  15  s  and  then  turn  it  off.  Remove  the  test  specimens  and 
wash  with  water.  Dip  In  hydrochloric  add  (  A-4J.1  )  for  1  to  2  s  and  rinse  again.  Dry  and  reweigh 
the  specimens  separately. 

Note -*  The  test  specimen  8  may  be  conveniently  suppotted  vertically  by  their  bottom  edges  with  two  hook- 
shaped  pieces  of  copper  wire  fastened  to  a  copper  bar  laid  across  a  2-litre  beaker  containing  the  stripping  solution, 
which  may  be  used  for  a  number  of  specimens.  The  cathodes,  consisting  of  two  pieces  of  sheet  lead,  may  be 
supported  on  each  side  of  the  test  specimen  by  the  edge  of  the  beaker.  A  6  V  automobile  battery  of  a  low  voltage 
rectifer  are  suitable  sources  of  current*  a  series  resistance  being  utilized  for  adjusting  the  current  to  4  A. 

U 


18:12313-1988 

A-4.3  Calculation  —The  loss  in  mass  in  grams  multiplied  by  400  is  equal  to  the  coating  mass 
in  grams  per  square  metre  of  sheet  when  a  specimen  of  2  500  mm*  in  area  is  used.  For  specimens  of 
other  sizes,  a  suitable  correction  factor  shall  be  applied. 

A-5.  Procedure  C  —  Stripping  with  Silver  Nitrate  Soiution 

A-5.1  Reagent 

A-5.1.1  Silver  nitrate  solution  —  Dissolve  200  g  of  silver  nitrate  (  AgNOs)  in  distilled  water  and 
dilute  to  1  litre. 

A-5.2  Procedure  for  Stripping 

A-5.2.1  After  cleaning  as  described  in  A-2.3,  weigh  each  test  specimen  separately.  Then  place 
in  a  beaker  containing  200  mi  of  the  silver  nitrate  solution  (  A-5.1  )  (  see  Note  ),  Reaction  is  fairly 
rapid.  The  terne  ( lead  alloy  )  coating  goes  into  solution  and  metallic  sliver  is  deposited  on  the 
surface  of  the  steel.  Remove  the  silver  by  washing  the  test  specimen  with  a  stream  of  water  from 
a  wash  bottle  and  rubbing  with  a  rubber-tipped  glass  rod. 

A-5.2.2  Examine  for  lead  spots.  If  any  are  found,  repeat  the  immersion  until  all  the  coating  is 
removed.  Then  thoroughly  wash  and  dry  the  test  specimen  and  reweigh. 

Note  —  The  silver  nitrate  solution  nriay  be  used  repeatedly  as  long  as  lead  Is  removed.  The  number  of  specimens 
that  can  be  stripped  with  200  mi  of  soiution  depends  on  the  amount  of  coating  on  the  sheets.  The  solution  is  used 
cold  and  replaced  with  fresh  soiution  when  the  reaction  becomes  too  slow.  After  the  first  specimen  is  stripped, 
silver  nitrate  solution  is  discoloured.  Most  of  the  silver  can  be  recovered  from  the  used  solution  and  washing,  if 
desired. 

A-5.3  Calculation  —The  loss  in  mass  in  grams  multiplied  by  400  is  equal  to  the  coating  mass 
in  grams  per  square  metre  of  sheet,  when  a  specimen  of  2  500  mm'  in  area  is  used.  For  specimens 
of  other  sizes,  a  suitable  correction  factor  shall  be  applied. 

A-6.  Procedure  D  —  Stripping  with  Hydrochloric  Acid  and  Antimony  (  ill  )  Chloride 

A-6.1  Reagent 

A-6.1.1  Antimony  ( /// )  Chloride  —Hydrochloric  Acid  Solution  —Dissolve  approximately  40  g  of 
antimony  (  III  )  chloride  (  SbCIs )  in  cp  or  reagent  grade  hydrochloric  acid  (  p  1.19  g/ml  )  and  dilute 
to  1  litre  with  the  hydrochloric  acid. 

A-6.2  Procedure  for  Stripping  —  After  cleaning  as  described  in  A-2.3,  weigh  each  test  specimen 
separately,  immerse  in  the  cold  antimony  (  III  )  chloride-hydrochloric  acid  soiution  (  A-6.1  )  until 
the  coating  is  removed  and  the  reaction  ceases.  The  reaction  will  leave  the  specimen  coated  with 
antimony.  Wash  thoroughly  to  remove  the  loosely  adherent  antimony,  dry  and  reweigh. 

A-6.3  Calculation  —  The  loss  in  mass  in  grams  multiplied  by  400  is  the  mass  of  coating  in  grams 
per  square  metre  of  sheet  when  a  specimen  of  2  500  mm>  In  area  Is  used.  For  specimens  of  other 
sizes,  a  suitable  correction  factor  shall  be  applied. 

A-7.  Procedure  E  —  Stripping  with  Sodium  Hydroxide  and  Sodium  Peroxide 

A-7*1  Reagents 

A-7.1.1  Sodium  hydroxide  solution  —5  percent  (  mjm  )  —  Dissolve  50  g  of  sodium  hydroxide 
(  NaOH  )  in  1  litre  of  water. 

A-7.1.2  Sodium  peroxide  —  granulated*. 

A.7tf2  Procedure  for  Stripping  —  After  cleaning  as  described  in  A-2.3,  weigh  each  test  specimen 
separately.  Fill  a  porcelain  dish  (  approximately  120  mm  in  diameter )  to  about  three-quarter 
capacity  with  sodium  hydroxide  solution  (  A-7.1.1  )  and  heat  to60''C  on  a  hot  plate.  Place  the  speci- 
men in  the  dish  making  sure  it  is  completely  immersed.  Slowly  add  the  granulated  sodium  peroxide 
(  A-7.1.2  )  until  the  solution  becomes  clear.  Turn  the  test  specimen  over  to  expose  the  other  side 
and  add  sodium  peroxide  until  the  solution  again  become  clear.  Stripping  Is  complete  when  no  more 
lead  is  detectable  on  the  specimen.  Discard  the  used  sodium  hydroxide  solution.  Carefully  rinsethe 
specimen  with  water,  dry  and  reweigh. 

A-7.3  Calculation  —  The  loss  in  mass  Ih  grams  multiplied  by  400  Is  the  mass  of  coating  In  grams 
per  square  metre  of  sheet  when  a  specimen  of  2  500  mm*  in  area  is  used.  For  specimens  of  other 
sizes,  a  suitable  correction  factor  shall  be  applied. 


*lt  is  important  to  use  only  granulated  sodium  peroxide. 

12 


IS:  12313 -1988 

EXPLANATORY     NOTE 

This  Standard  applies  to  cold-rolled  carbon  steel  sheet  of  the  drawing  qualities  coated  by  a 
continuous  hot-dip  terne  ( lead  alloy  )  coating  process,  it  includes  that  group  of  products  commonly 
known  as  terne  plate  or  terne  sheets.  Terne  sheets  are  used  where  ease  of  soiderablllty,  a  degree 
of  corrosion  resistance,  or  amenability  to  stamping,  pressing  or  deep-drawing  will  be  advantageous. 
The  mass  of  coating  may  be  specified  in  accordance  with  Table  2.  It  is  expressed  as  the  total  coating 
on  both  surfaces  In  grams  per  square  metre.  The  coating  mass  specified  should  be  compatible 
with  the  desired  service  life,  thicliness  of  the  base  metal  and  the  forming  requirements  involved. 
A  designation  system  (  see  2.3 )  includes  the  coating  designation,  coating  condition  and  quality. 

Terne  sheet  Is  normally  produced  in  the  range  of  thicliness  0*30  to  20  mm  inclusive,  and  In 
widths  up  to  1  400  mm  in  coils  and  cut  lengths.  Terne  sheet  less  than  600  mm  wide  may  be  slit  from 
wide  sheet  and  will  be  considered  as  sheet. 

Ordinary  quality  terne  sheet  ( TO  01 )  is  intended  for  general  fabricating  purposes  where  sheet  is 
used  in  the  flat  or  for  bending  or  moderate  forming. 

Drawing  quality  terne  sheet  (  TO  02,  TO  03  and  TO  04  )  is  intended  for  drawing  or  severe  forming 
It  Is  furnished  to  all  the  requirements  of  this  standard  or  with  agreement,  when  ordered,  to  fabri- 
cate an  identified  part,  in  which  case  the  mechanical  properties  in  Table  3  do  not  apply.  Drawing 
qualities  are  identified  as  follows: 

TO  02  Drawing  quality 

TO  03  Deep  drawing  quality 

TO  04  Extra  deep  drawing  quality  special  killed 

Terne  sheet  is  suitable  for  welding,  soldering  or  brazing,  if  appropriate  methods  and  proce- 
dures are  selected  with  special  attention  to  the  heavier  coatings.  When  sheet  is  subjected  to  join- 
ing techniques  Involving  heat,  suitable  precautions  shall  be  taken  to  avoid  toxic  affects. 

This  standard  Is  in  agreement  with  the  ISO  4999-1978  Hot-Dip  Terne  Coated  Carbon  Steel 
Sheets,  issued  by  the  International  Organization  for  Standardization  (  ISO  ),
